mood.instructions: The dominant emotional tone of the post as a whole.

criteria.hopeful: optimistic, excited, sees things getting better
criteria.worried: anxious, uneasy, warns about where things are heading
criteria.angry: frustrated, indignant, pushes back against something
criteria.reflective: contemplative, weighing things, thinking out loud without a strong emotion
criteria.playful: light, humorous, having fun with the topic
criteria.matter_of_fact: neutral and explanatory, reports or explains without much feeling

scale.instructions: Whose world the post is mostly about.

criteria.self: the author himself, his life and feelings
criteria.craft: the daily work of programming and its tools
criteria.community: open source projects and communities and the people in them
criteria.society: society at large, politics, culture, humanity

criteria.past: looks back: history, how things were, lessons learned
criteria.present: describes how things are right now
criteria.future: looks ahead: what will or should happen

ai.instructions: If the post is about AI, which part of it.

criteria.agents: coding agents and working with them day to day
criteria.models: what models can do, how they behave or reason, model releases
criteria.local: local or open-weight models and the hardware to run them
criteria.society: AI's effect on society, politics, jobs, regulation
criteria.community: AI's effect on open source, communities and collaboration
criteria.writing: AI-generated text and content, authenticity, slop
criteria.risk: AI safety, doom, loss of control
criteria.not_ai: the post is not mainly about AI

imagery.instructions: Look only at the title and at the metaphors and images the author himself uses in the text (not at the topic). Which family of images do they come from? Software, computers and code are the topic, not imagery: answer 'none' unless the author actually uses a figurative image.

criteria.water: sea, river, rain, waves, flow, flood, drowning, ships
criteria.air: sky, clouds, fog, wind, ghosts, the intangible
criteria.growth: plants, trees, gardens, roots, harvest, seasons, things taking time to grow
criteria.building: towers, houses, cities, towns, walls, construction
criteria.road: paths, journeys, crossings, maps, borders, divides
criteria.light: stars, sun, lamps, darkness and light
criteria.body: illness, madness, the body, the senses
criteria.crowd: people, tribes, gatherings, a lone figure
criteria.none: the author uses no figurative imagery worth mentioning

stance.instructions: The role the author takes in this post.

criteria.builder: shows something he made and how
criteria.teacher: explains how something works or how to do it
criteria.advocate: argues for something, tries to convince
criteria.observer: describes and weighs what he sees without taking a firm side
criteria.witness: tells what happened to him personally

actor.instructions: Who or what drives the events the post talks about.

criteria.individual: a single person, usually the author
criteria.group: a community, a team, a movement
criteria.machine: software, tools or AI acting on their own
criteria.idea: nobody in particular: a technique, a design, an idea

criteria.resolved: with a firm conclusion or verdict
criteria.open: with a question, doubt or unresolved thought
criteria.call: with a call to the reader to do something
criteria.practical: with a practical wrap-up: links, next steps, a summary of what to use

tension.instructions: How much the post is about a conflict between opposing forces or groups.
criteria: the conflict is the whole post

valence.instructions: How bright or dark the outlook of the post is.

criteria: a clear line with some detours
freely associative, wandering from thought to thought
largely about the author's own life or feelings

humor.instructions: How much humour there is in the writing.

criteria: deeply technical, mostly code and internals
